column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the river simply “the River” and repeats “father” for Terah’s relation to Abraham and Nahor; BSB specifies “the Euphrates” and states “father” once.
The Hebrew says “the River” and uses the image of Abraham’s “seed”; BSB specifies “the Euphrates” and says “descendants.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names “Egypt” and says “in its midst”; BSB has “the Egyptians” and “there.”
The Hebrew first says only “the sea,” later naming the Sea of Reeds, and repeats “your fathers”; BSB calls the sea “Red Sea” both times and uses “them” for the second reference to the fathers.
The Hebrew begins with “they” and describes the sea coming over and covering a singular collective recipient; BSB supplies “your fathers” and uses plural “them.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amorite” and states the possession and destruction as successive clauses; BSB has plural “Amorites” and subordinates them with “that” and “when.”
The Hebrew says Balak rose and fought against Israel; BSB expresses this as “set out to fight.”
The Hebrew repeats the blessing verb for emphasis; BSB expresses this as blessing “again and again.”
The Hebrew calls Jericho’s people its “lords” or owners and uses singular collective names for the seven peoples; BSB has “the people” and plural ethnic names.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew shifts to singular “you” for laboring on the land, then back to plural “you” for building and planting; BSB uses the same English pronoun throughout.
The Hebrew says “the River” without explicitly naming it; BSB specifies “the Euphrates.”
The Hebrew says “evil in your eyes,” names “the River,” and uses singular collective “the Amorite”; BSB has “unpleasing in your sight,” specifies “the Euphrates,” and uses plural “Amorites.”
The Hebrew has both “answered” and “said”; BSB gives a single “replied.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amorite”; BSB has plural “the Amorites.”
The Hebrew says God will not “lift” the transgressions and sins and joins them with “and”; BSB has “forgive” and “or.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Joshua as the person addressed; BSB leaves him implicit.
The Hebrew says they chose the LORD “for yourselves, to serve Him”; BSB combines this as choosing “to serve the LORD.” The Hebrew reply is simply “Witnesses”; BSB supplies “We are.”
The Hebrew uses singular “your heart”; BSB has plural “your hearts.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the image of cutting the covenant and refers to the people with a singular pronoun; BSB says “made a covenant” and uses plural “them.”
The Hebrew says the tree was “in” the LORD’s sanctuary; BSB says it was “near” the sanctuary.
The Hebrew says “lest you deny” your God; BSB recasts this as “if you ever deny.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “after these things” and describes the age as a “son of a hundred and ten years”; BSB has “Some time later” and “at the age of 110.”
Close to the Hebrew.
